category: Online storefront and order rail for small shops
oneLiner: Tapstall gives a shop one link: the customer taps it, picks, and pays the exact amount, and the order lands in a dashboard the shop owns.
definition: Tapstall is a store-link and order rail for small retailers in Zimbabwe and South Africa, built for Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram sellers whose orders were previously scattered across chat.
audience: Small shops and social sellers in Zimbabwe and South Africa

features.name: Menu first
features.detail: Put the products and prices in once.

features.name: Share the link
features.detail: Post it where you already sell, including WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.

features.name: Exact amounts
features.detail: The customer pays the exact amount, so the payment matches the order.

features.name: Dashboard
features.detail: Name, number, address, items and amount land in an order list the shop owns.

features.name: Local payments
features.detail: EcoCash, InnBucks, PayShap and ZIPIT are the expected rails.

features.name: No order cap
features.detail: No commission on orders and no hostage data.

outcomes: One link that works in any chat app
Orders written down instead of remembered
Payments matched to the order that caused them
Data the shop owns, exportable to its own Google Sheet

faqs.question: What is Tapstall?
faqs.answer: Tapstall is a store link for small shops: a customer taps it, picks from the menu and pays the exact amount, and the order arrives in a dashboard the shop owns.

faqs.question: How much does Tapstall cost?
faqs.answer: It is free for 60 days with no card. After that it is $7 a month or $60 a year, or R129 a month or R999 a year in South Africa.

faqs.question: Which payments does Tapstall work with?
faqs.answer: The shops it is built for use EcoCash, InnBucks, PayShap and ZIPIT, alongside ordinary bank transfers.

faqs.question: Does Tapstall take a commission?
faqs.answer: No. There is no order cap and no commission; the shop keeps its own order data and can export it to its own Google Sheet.

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a store?
faqs.answer: About 90 seconds: put the menu in, share the link, and start taking orders from the chat apps the shop already sells in.

faqs.question: Does a customer need to install an app?
faqs.answer: No. The store is a page behind a link, so it opens in whatever browser the customer already has.

faqs.question: Why not just use Shopify?
faqs.answer: Shopify and the platforms built for Silicon Valley assume cards, couriers and a checkout flow that many shops in Zimbabwe and South Africa do not have. Tapstall is built around local payment rails and chat-based selling.

faqs.question: Who is Tapstall for?
faqs.answer: Small retailers and social sellers in Zimbabwe and South Africa, especially those taking orders through WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
